title: When the Undertow Breaks
premise: Juniper Delacroix, a night librarian who has spent twelve years almost confessing their love to the archivist Odile, is summoned by Maren Voss, the last fluent speaker of Kessuwan, a dying language of tidal marshes. Maren's final lesson becomes a reckoning: the language holds an inheritance ritual that can only be passed at the place where her own story broke — the flooded village of Saint-Aubin, which she abandoned during a storm that killed her sister. As Juniper and Odile travel with Maren, Juniper must finally speak what they have withheld, learning that survival without speech is its own kind of drowning. The book ends at Saint-Aubin's ruined chapel, where Maren dies mid-lesson and Juniper, now the second-to-last speaker, completes the ritual aloud — choosing inheritance over the safety of silence.
about_author: Mirabel Almeida is a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing endangered oral histories along the Atlantic coast. She writes from a converted oyster shed in Nova Scotia, where the tide dictates her working hours.

chapters.title: The Hours We Keep Awake
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. In the sleepless night library, Juniper catalogs damaged books while orbiting Odile, rehearsing confessions they never deliver. Maren Voss arrives at 3 a.m., asking for 'one final student,' and names Juniper specifically. Emotional beat: restless longing interrupted by fate; the first crack in Juniper's careful routine of almost-saying.

chapters.title: Lessons in a Drowning Tongue
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, with Maren's recorded voice threaded through. Daily lessons reveal Kessuwan's grammar of tide and debt, and Maren's condition: the last lesson happens only at Saint-Aubin. Odile insists on coming, forcing proximity Juniper both craves and fears. Emotional beat: intimacy through language, terror of the destination, rising dread as Maren weakens.

chapters.title: What the Water Kept
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. At half-drowned Saint-Aubin, Maren finally tells the truth: she survived the storm by not answering her sister's call, and the language itself carries that guilt — words for things unsaid outnumber words for things done. A flood traps them overnight; Juniper nearly loses Odile and blurts the confession mid-crisis. Emotional beat: climax — secrets break open as literally as the levee does.

chapters.title: Second-to-Last Speaker
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. In the ruined chapel, Maren begins the inheritance ritual but dies before its final line. Grieving, Juniper must reconstruct it alone — and realizes the missing phrase is the one they've practiced for twelve years: saying the true thing aloud. They finish the ritual, speaking to Odile plainly for the first time. Emotional beat: sorrow transmuted into inheritance; silence finally broken.
